title: Stamp 1: Immigration History
welcome_lead: Stamp France's history of immigration into your passport.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on immigration history from the Maghreb, Africa, and Asia.

concepts.def: Migration from Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia, especially after WWII and decolonisation.
Migration from sub-Saharan African countries, growing since the 1970s.
Migration from former Indochina (Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos), particularly post-1975.
Post-war economic boom (1945-1975) drawing labour from abroad.
Family reunification, formally allowed from 1976 after 1974 immigration freeze.
Second generation: children of immigrants born in France.

walkthroughs.body_html: During the Trente Glorieuses, France recruited workers from southern Europe (Italy, Portugal, Spain) and the Maghreb to fuel reconstruction. The 1973 oil crisis ended this open phase.
After 1975, France welcomed refugees fleeing communist regimes in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Laos. They became known as the boat people. The community settled around the 13th arrondissement of Paris.
Un immigre = immigrant. Un naturalise = naturalised citizen. Le droit du sol = jus soli. Le droit du sang = jus sanguinis.
